value.description: Throw three quills with microscopic, backward-facing barbs that are difficult to remove once embedded in flesh.
Throw three quills with microscopic, backward-facing barbs that are difficult to remove once embedded in flesh.
Fire a volley of ionized plasma projectiles.

All insectoids were created to fight mechanoids. The black hive were the best of the best, an insectoid hive so vicious and so terrifying that any mechanoids would flee when encountering them. That, however, was many years ago. Nowadays remnants of the black hive roam various planets, a latent menace to anyone using advanced technology.
A bloodshot eye with a triangular pupil. This horrible mutant eye confers the gift of improved psychic sight.
A weird mutant eye that is never fully open, being partially covered by a sickly looking eyelid. Strangely enough, it provides normal sight while protecting its host from psychic attacks.
A splash of acid that continues to cause burn wounds for quite some time after the initial attack.
The summit crab will instantly flatten anything that gets in front of it.
A fast acting toxin is coursing through this creature's veins, paralyzing the muscles. It will wear off after a while.

Toxins in the bloodstream. This can come from various sources, including environmental toxins, venomous bites, or poisoned weapons. At high doses, toxic buildup is lethal. Even at low doses, it can generate cancers. Creatures who die with this toxic damage can still be eaten.
This angel moth has recently consumed clothes of legendary quality.
This sand squid has recently fertilized some sandy terrain.

This creature has been affected by swarmling implantation. If the disease is not properly treated, or if the creature dies when it is sufficiently advanced, swarmling larvae will devour it from inside and hatch from its corpse.
This animal survived a fatal wound, coming back from the dead.
This sand prowler is burrowing under the sand, making it very resistant to damage.

A fungal infection in a wound. Without treatment, the infection will advance at an astonishing rate, killing the afflicted in a few hours. It is very easy to treat, and it will be kept contained and disappear as long as it is treated fast and effectively.
A fresh corpse has been consumed and will provide the erin with a considerable health boost for almost half a day.
Extract uranium from unrefined uranium crystals.

value.letterText: A darkbeast has died nearby, releasing a cloud of sun-blocking mechanites.\n\nThese mechanites will block sunlight, plunging the whole region into darkness. They will eventually dissipate and it will be shorter than a natural eclipse.

value.description: This standard issue drop pod seems to have been modified to host a small self-contained ecosystem. As soon as it impacted, strange creeping vines and weird creatures emerged from it. It seems to be some kind of terraforming machine.\n\nYou can destroy it to avoid the release of potentially hostile lifeforms into this region, or wait until its work is done to see what happens.
A hive of giant insects. This mound was used by the black hive to tunnel to this territory, and is now inert. It will erode in a few days.
A rock full of very hard and resilient mineral originating from space.
White thick leather covered in a long, rugged mat of fur. Harvested from an arctic lion. This thick skin insulates from cold and protects really well.
This furry hide is of exceptional quality. Possibly one of the best leathers obtainable.
A coarse tan wool with long fibers and a pseudo-crystalline lattice of organic support structures underneath. Quite strong and very good at keeping the desert heat out.
A very tough silk extracted from angel moths. Very poor insulator.
A soft silk produced by the giant crowned silkie. Once woven, it is very similar to, but softer than sheep wool. Considered a luxury item.
These quills are coated with a powerful anesthetic and can be used as an alternative to herbal medicines. Not as powerful as industrial medicine but useful in an emergency situation.
Milk substitute from a frostbound behemoth. Very nutritious but the bluish color is more than a little unsettling.
Milk from a spined gow. Very nutritious but the reddish color is a little unsettling.

A synthetic mixture of protein, carbohydrates, and vitamins, amino acids and minerals. Everything the body needs, and absolutely disgusting. This paste is even worse than the paste produced by a nutrient paste dispenser and people will hate eating it. It is cheap, though!\n\nIt is completely indigestible for herbivores.
A gallatross' horn. This rock-hard horn is very valuable, and given the dangers inherent in hunting a gallatross, a scarce commodity.
A syrupy residue extracted from aerofleets that can be refined into an energy-dense compound. The compound can be used to build powerful batteries and generators.

A crystallized and condensed variety of blue gel. Hexagel is capable of storing much more energy, but it also seems to be quite unstable. Hexagel can be used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropiate research.
A hexagonal shaped energy core composed of already highly unstable hydrogen-rich blue gel stabilized within a uranium shell.
Raw agarilux harvested from an agaripod. It is very nice to eat, even when raw.
Very nutritious but the jet-black color is more than a little unsettling.
Raw butchered flesh from an aerofleet. Chewy, gelatinous, and insipid. Similar in texture to jellyfish.
Raw butchered flesh from an ocular jelly. Chewy, gelatinous, and insipid. Similar in texture to jellyfish.
Raw red slime. This stuff is edible. Barely.

Jelly stored and used as food by oversized insects. It is smooth, rich, and fulfills the recreation need of those who consume it. Because of its unique biological properties, it can nourish almost any creature and never rots. This particular insect jelly is pitch black in color and seems to be more nutritious than usual.\n\nOddly, its texture and nutrient blanace makes it an ideal baby food.
Fertilized bumbledrone eggs. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby bumbledrone. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
Fertilized wildpod spores. If all goes well, it should bud into a baby wildpod. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
Fertilized agaripod spores. If all goes well, it should bud into a baby agaripod. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
Fertilized mycoid colossus spores. If all goes well, it should bud into a baby mycoid colossus. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
Fertilized wildpawn spores. If all goes well, it should bud into a baby wildpawn. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
Fertilized agaripawn spores. If all goes well, it should bud into a baby agaripawn. It can be eaten raw, and isn't much better cooked.
An unfertilized ironhusk beetle egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized ironhusk beetle egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby ironhusk beetle. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized mammoth worm egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized mammoth worm egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby mammoth worm. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized crepuscular beetle egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized crepuscular beetle egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby crepuscular beetle. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized great devourer egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized great devourer egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby great devourer. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a worm egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized megalouse egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a louse egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized megalouse egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby megalouse. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a louse egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized bedbug egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized bedbug egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby bedbug. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a beetle egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized animalisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby animalisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...
An unfertilized lisk species egg. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized feralisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby feralisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...

A fertilized feralisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby feralisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...\n\nThis egg seems to be developing at an alarmingly accelerated rate!
A fertilized dunealisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby dunealisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...

A fertilized dunealisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby dunealisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...\n\nThis egg seems to be developing at an alarmingly accelerated rate!
A fertilized blizzarisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby blizzarisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...

A fertilized blizzarisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby blizzarisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...\n\nThis egg seems to be developing at an alarmingly accelerated rate!
A fertilized junglelisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a junglelisk. Inedible.
A fertilized cinderlisk egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby cinderlisk. It can be eaten raw or cooked, but it's a spider egg, so it's disgusting either way...
A fertilized nightling egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby nightling. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized nightling egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized meadow ave egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby meadow ave. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized ave egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized desert ave egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby desert ave. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized night ave egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby night ave. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized royal ave egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby royal ave. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

A fertilized rough-plated monitor egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby rough-plated monitor. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked. Rough-plated monitor eggs are violently unstable, and they explode when they hatch!
A fertilized atispec egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into an atispec larva. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized atispec egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized angel moth egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into an angel moth larva. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized butterfly egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized drainer egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a drainer larva. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.

A fertilized fire wasp egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby fire wasp. It is extremely uncomfortable to eat. Fire wasp eggs radiate an incredible amount of heat, and can be dangerous if left unchecked.
An unfertilized fire wasp egg. It is extremely uncomfortable to eat. Fire wasp eggs radiate an incredible amount of heat, and can be dangerous if left unchecked.
A fertilized flamingo phoenix egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a flamingo phoenix chick. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized crescendo anole egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby crescendo anole. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized crescendo anole egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized pedigreed raptor egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a baby pedigreed raptor. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
An unfertilized pedigreed raptor egg. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized empress butterfly egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into an empress butterfly larva. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A fertilized giant crowned silkie egg. If all goes well, it should hatch into a giant crowned silkie chick. It can be eaten raw, but it's much better cooked.
A bloodshot eye with a triangular pupil. This horrible mutant eye confers the gift of improved psychic sight.
A weird mutant eye that is never fully open, being partially covered by a sickly looking eyelid. Strangely enough, it provides normal sight while protecting its host from psychic attacks.

This tree is completely otherworldly, probably not even 100% carbon based, and it seems to be struggling to grow from exposure to a terrestrial environment. Strange fruits resembling eyeballs hang from the tree but they are inedible. Its wood releases a powerful, sweet scent.

A huge unicellular organism genetically modified to serve as a biological cleaning machine. They will feed on most types of non-metallic trash, engorging themselves in the process.\n\nAfter a certain amount of feedings, acanthamoeba giganteas will increase in size and eventually split into two different individuals. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A huge unicellular organism genetically modified to serve as a biological cleaning machine. They will feed on most types of non-metallic trash, engorging themselves in the process.\n\nAfter a certain amount of feedings, acanthamoeba giganteas will increase in size and eventually split into two different individuals. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A huge unicellular organism genetically modified to serve as a biological cleaning machine. They will feed on most types of non-metallic trash, engorging themselves in the process.\n\nAfter a certain amount of feedings, acanthamoeba giganteas will increase in size and eventually split into two different individuals. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A small, floating gelatinous creature propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter. These squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, Aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

Aerofleets slowly produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as blue gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound. The compound can be used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research.

A huge, floating gelatinous creature propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter. These squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

This aerofleet has somehow grown to extreme size. A small number of younger aerofleets seem to be attracted to it and follow it everywhere.

Colossal aerofleets produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as blue gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound. The compound can be used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research.

A subspecies of wildpawn that has grown in the secluded environment of a mycotic jungle. Its body is covered by agarilux mushrooms that seem to be in a state of symbiosis. Agaripawns are less resistant to gunfire than agaripods but still retain a weakness to fire. Agaripawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so their children are completely wild and independent of them, with no concept of parenthood. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.\n\nAgaripawns can be hunted or farmed for small amounts of edible raw agarilux, which can be eaten raw and rots slower than regular fungus.

A subspecies of wildpod that has grown in the secluded environment of a mycotic jungle. Its body is covered by agarilux mushrooms that seem to be in a state of symbiosis. Agaripods are almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass. In contrast, they are very weak to fire. Agripods reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so their children are completely wild and independent of them, with no concept of parenthood. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.\n\nAlthough risky, agaripods can be hunted or farmed for decent amounts of edible raw agarilux, which can be eaten raw and rots slower than regular fungus.

A genetically engineered lepidopteran that was a product of a waste disposal experiment being abandoned and its subjects being released into the wild. Angel moth larvae are timid and harmless. They are content with munching on sparse vegetation and will eventually metamorphose into its adult form.

Adult angel moths are voracious and will mainly consume clothing and textiles. If no clothes are present, they'll reluctantly eat grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are unruly creatures.

Adults produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile. Care must be taken to keep it out of other angel moths' reach, since they can consume it too.

A genetically engineered lepidopteran that was a product of a waste disposal experiment being abandoned and its subjects being released into the wild.

Angel moths are voracious and will mainly consume clothing and textiles. If no clothes are present, they'll reluctantly eat grass. Although they can be used to get rid of unwanted clothing, it is hard to make them discriminate, as they are unruly creatures.

They produce a moth silk that can be harvested to use as a textile. Care must be taken to keep it out of other angel moths' reach, since they can consume it too.

A variant of the overgrown colossus native to anima forests. They are reptilian in nature, with cold blood and a slow metabolism. They have six legs, two intertwined spines, and six eyes.

It has a symbiotic relationship with anima vegetation, with several anima trees and mystic cap mushrooms growing on its back. These plants seem to provide sustenance in a symbiotic relationship with the colossus.

When tamed, the anima colossus can be periodically trimmed to obtain wood. It will also very rarely produce a huge, hardened anima pearl, which can be planted to grow a new anima tree.

A psionically gifted variation of feralisks, most likely artificially mutated, adapted to living in anima forests. Animalisks are the only herbivorous species of lisks, so they aren't as dangerous as the rest of their kin. They consume anima grass and anima trees as a part of their diet.\n\nAnimalisks defend themselves by throwing huge webs at their harassers. These webs stun anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

A small canine with latent psionic abilities. It is intelligent for an animal but not intelligent enough to properly use psionics. It will quickly bond with human beings and reach with its mind to make everyone that treats it well happy.\n\nAnimus voxes are often seen as pets, though some wander the wilderness looking for someone to bond to.

A descendant of the lion that were specifically engineered as ambush units for extremely low temperature environments. Even though its danger and capabilities are common knowledge, many people still attempt to hunt them for their unique light reflecting fur and tough leather that provides surprisingly high thermal insulation.

A strange semi-insectoid creature that undergoes radical metamorphosis, similar to butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are harmless medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and are usually preyed upon. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.\n\nAdult atispecs are huge, carnivorous, and venomous flying predators. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult atispecs but it is not as effective as growing them during their 2 year long phase as a larva.

A strange semi-insectoid creature that undergoes radical metamorphosis, similar to butterflies. Atispecs are huge, carnivorous, and venomous flying predators. There have been attempts to domesticate the adult atispecs but it is not as effective as growing them during their 2 year long phase as a larva.

A wispy-looking creature that is the only known example of plasma-based life. It is believed that they were created as a lifeform capable of surviving in the atmosphere of red dwarf stars, for utterly inscrutable purposes.\n\nAurora sylphs don't seem to be affected by gravity much, so they can also be found stranded in the gravity well of a planet. They are immune to temperature extremes and the vacuum of space, though very fragile and easy to damage. They don't need to eat, as they will replenish their energy simply by absorbing light. If they are content, they will periodically influence the magnetic fields of a planet and cause beautiful auroras.

A large genetically-modified scorpion. No one really knows where they came from, but judging by its ability to rip apart living things within reach and pierce those outside of it, it’s a monster made for war.

An oversized pest and a nuisance in every world they manage to infest. While not particularly dangerous or powerful on their own, their bite carries a powerful toxin that paralyzes its prey, so one small bite is enough to down prey much larger than themselves.

A forsaken creature believed to reside in the outer star belts. Legends speak of these incredibly intelligent and fierce behemoths, ruling over whole planets with their devastating fire breaths and incomprehensible power.\n\nBehemoths were used as powerful beasts of burden by the forsaken. They can spew flames from their mouth and regenerate their wounds quite fast.

A large genetically-engineered beetle that is a part of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The black hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created to increase its lethality.\n\nBlack scarabs are little more than cannon fodder, released ahead of the main insectoid horde to draw enemy fire. A eusocial creature, it cannot reproduce individually. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.

A bioengineered insectoid the size of a sheep. It is a part of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The black hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created to increase its lethality.\n\nThe spelopede is the middle caste of a hive, taking care of most work tasks as well as fighting with its digging claws. It's dangerous in combat, but slow on open ground. Its ranged attacks cause acidic damage to mechanoids and toxic damage to living creatures.

A genetically-engineered insectoid the size of a bear. This creature is a part of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The black hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created to increase its lethality.\n\nThe blackspider is designed for heavy work and combat. Its thick chitinous armor makes it hard to kill, while its long ripper-blades make it deadly at close quarters. Its ranged attacks cause acidic damage to mechanoids and toxic damage to living creatures.

A mutant variation of the feralisk that has adapted to extremely cold climates. Blizzarisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs both stun and freeze anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

A mutant variation of the feralisk that has adapted to extremely cold climates. Blizzarisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs both stun and freeze anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.\n\nThis blizzarisk is larger than usual, and is carrying a clutch of eggs on its back. This sounds like a recipe for disaster if not dealt with quickly.

A smaller relative of the raptor shrimp, the blood shrimp lacks the impressive regenerative abilities of its larger counterpart. They compensate this disadvantage by being faster and more agile.\n\nBlood shrimps are vampiric, feeding on blood and being able to regenerate their wounds when drinking the blood of live animals.

A huge insect engineered to feed on the gigantic flowers of a utopian idyllic meadow. Although based on an insectoid geneline, they have been carefully designed to produce meat that is virtually indistinguishable from beef.\n\nBobeenes are peaceful, unintelligent beasts that are content with buzzing around the meadows, and make for excellent dairy cattle and pack animals. They hover over terrain, thus ignoring movement costs.

A large genetically-engineered crab which uses a boulder for a shell. It is alternatively known as the atlas crab throughout various colonized planets. These massive creatures sport incredible strength and are commonly seen carrying giant boulders that would normally crush living things and machinery alike.\n\nDespite first impressions, it is quite peaceful, preferring to ignore any form of assault it may receive. Its predators are more likely to die of old age than to take down such an armored creature.

Legends tell of a great bouldermit that had grown so large and so powerful that it used entire mountains for a home. This summit crab probably isn't the sole originator of such tales, but it is a fine example of a creature people certainly don't want to encounter as will crush anything that happens to be in its path.

A mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a bumbledrone isn't very powerful, but in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. Since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method.\n\nAs a floating creature, bumbledrones ignore terrain movement costs.

A mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a bumbledrone isn't very powerful, but in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. Since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method.

Each colony has a few bumbledrones that develop further into powerful killing machines called bumbledrone hierophants. Aside from their nasty venom, hierophants are armed with a pair of vicious claws that take quick care of any enemies of the colony.

As a floating creature, bumbledrone hierophants ignore terrain movement costs.

A mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a bumbledrone isn't very powerful, but in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. Since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rather than as a hunting method.\n\nThe bumbledrone queen lays eggs once it has settled into an environment it considers safe. As a floating creature, bumbledrone queens ignore terrain movement costs.

In an effort to make deserts more viable for colonization, scientists introduced a variety of genetically modified creatures that are made to survive the melting heat and provide food to those who wished to live in such harsh conditions. One such creature is the cactipine. Despite its name, it is actually a giant rat infused with the DNA of a cactus. It resulted in the specimen gaining sharp medical quills, hardened green skin, and a funny tasting "meat" that confuses vegetarians and carnivores alike.

A long-haired domesticated bovid that has evolved a survival mechanism to camouflage itself in response to different stimuli. It changes its very metabolism according to the environment it is inhabiting at the time.\n\nChameleon yaks will change their temperature tolerance depending on their environment and even produce different types of wool. This change occurs at the cellular level and is very fast, but doesn't harm the animal in the slightest.

An ant-like creature created as a replacement for the ubiquitous boomalope. Chemfuel myrmidons consume both meat and vegetables to ferment them into a powerful chemfuel mixture, which can be periodically extracted from the animal.\n\nContrary to the boomalope, chemfuel myrmidons are resistant to damage, especially damage caused by high temperatures. They are perfectly content living in red-hot semi liquid ground.

A huge spider adapted to living close to the calderas of dormant volcanoes. They were originally engineered for their durable and heat-resistant silk, but once they escaped into the wild they began multiplying uncontrollably.\n\nCinderlisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs stun and burn anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome fangs. Their fangs are also burning-hot and can light things on fire.

A very large peaceful herbivore that originated from a mysterious rimworld orbiting a very faint star, perpetually covered in darkness. This was the home planet of an elusive race known as the forsaken, and crepuscular beetles were often used as domesticated beasts of burden.\n\nCrepuscular beetles are active during dusk and don't need a lot of rest, expending much less time than other creatures to replenish their energy.

A generally harmless iguanian lizard that feeds on vegetation and small arthropods. They are unusually intelligent and can be kept as pets.\n\nWhen the crescendo anole becomes aggressive in any way, usually in self defense, an unstable cocktail of growth hormones and biomechanical mechanites causes a runaway growth of the creature's cells, turning it into a hulking crocodilian nightmare. This effect is temporary, lasting a few hours, and afterwards the anole must recover its strength to be able to go through it again, becoming extremely hungry in the interim.

A heavily modified medium-sized wild cat, the crystalline caracal can be seen lazying around in the sun, recharging its internal energy. It can later use this stored energy to release a powerful blast of concentrated light. Typically nocturnal, they are highly secretive, territorial, and difficult to observe.\n\nContrary to other purely photosynthetic creatures, they can also hunt small prey, and it needs both kinds of sustenance to survive.

A pebblemit that has been genetically modified to feed on minerals. Crystalmits have a partly silicon-based biology, so they can derive sustenance from eating scattered rocks.\n\nCrystalmits were created as a quick way of removing rock rubble from mining operations, but wild ones may prove to be a nuisance for colonies who'd rather use rocks for something useful.

A mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with metallic spikes housing a distributed cloud of sun-blocking mechanites.\n\nThese deployable mechanite clouds can cover a huge region, blanketing it in darkness, and it is thought that the darkbeast was created as a terrorist weapon to attack settlements by depriving them of sunlight, affecting their agricultural yields. Darkbeasts have naturally evolved over the centuries making them extremely unstable and they will only release enough mechanites upon death. Predators usually give them a wide berth.

A creature of pure muscle that has incredible strength. Often seen foraging in groups among the undergrowth, they are renowned for their fiercely protective behavior over other members of their brood. Once provoked, the resulting rampage is the last thing many colonies see before their destruction under the might of an enraged pack. Despite its infamous reputation, the beast is still hunted often, not only for their thick hide or ample supply of meat, but also by warrior societies as a rite of passage.\n\nDark vandals can dig for truffles if they are hungry. They can only do so when on top of a diggable terrain.

A large, winged flightless lizard that inhabit places with abundant vegetation. Decay drakes release a nauseous cocktail of volatile pheromones that quickly accelerates the rotting process of plants, turning vegetation around them into mounds of fermented organic matter. They will consume these and usually get incredibly drunk in the process. They have four separate livers in order to process the huge amounts of alcohol.\n\nThey aren't easy to domesticate, but if they can be coerced to accept humans, they might be useful hunting companions, especially if provided with alcohol. Humans have been known to consume the rotting vegetation they generate in desperate times, but most people would rather starve.

A large flightless bird adapted to living in very arid terrains. Large bony plates cover its neck, giving it defense both from predators and from the scalding heat of the desert sun. Compared to their more common meadow ave relatives, desert aves are less temperamental, but their slightly smaller size makes them less useful as pack animals.\n\nDesert Aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

A genetically engineered sheep capable of producing extremely strong and valuable red wool. Some see it as a simple livestock. Others, a demonic entity of corruption.\n\nLike devilstrand mushrooms, these sheep take some time to grow the fabric, but they can be easily bred to increase production.

A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in one of the many toxic worlds that exist. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity.\n\nDrainers undergo metamorphosis like most other lepidopterans, though their larval stage is pretty short, and doesn't have the energy draining abilities of the adults.

A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in one of the many toxic worlds that exist. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity.\n\nDrainers undergo metamorphosis like most other lepidopterans, though their larval stage is pretty short, and doesn't have the energy draining abilities of the adults.

A mutant variation of the feralisk that has adapted to extremely hot climates. Dunealisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs both stun and burn anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

A mutant variation of the feralisk that has adapted to extremely hot climates. Dunealisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs both stun and burn anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.\n\nThis dunealisk is larger than usual, and is carrying a clutch of eggs on its back. This sounds like a recipe for disaster if not dealt with quickly.

A result of failed animal weaponization trials, it is an ideal killing machine, built and modified to satisfy the requirements of fast-paced warfare. The fierce nature of the night prowler is reinforced further by the muscular protrusions on their back, which simultaneously act as both accelerators and as weapons.\n\nTheir capability to overrun even the most well defended military facilities resulted in the systematic purge that was commissioned by some intergalactic federations centuries ago, in hopes of driving the prowlers to extinction. Thus, very few prowler sightings are reported nowadays.

A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.\n\nThis rat seems to be different from other rats. It is purely nocturnal and has four glowing eyes.

A butterfly that originated from an extremely rare type of planet – a paradise glitterworld. These planets have reached an extreme level of technology, but their inhabitants are very psychically sensitive, using their technology to offset any impact they might have on the planet's ecosystem and thereby anima. The empress butterfly was engineered as the perfect pollinator. They gather pollen from genetically engineered plants that increase the fertility of the surrounding terrain and release it nearby.\n\nLarvae are small, slow, and practically useless but they have no special dietary constraints.

A butterfly that originated from an extremely rare type of planet – a paradise glitterworld. These planets have reached an extreme level of technology, but their inhabitants are very psychically sensitive, using their technology to offset any impact they might have on the planet's ecosystem and thereby anima. The empress butterfly was engineered as the perfect pollinator. They gather pollen from genetically engineered plants that increase the fertility of the surrounding terrain and release it nearby.\n\nAdult empress butterflies have strict dietary constraints, as they demand a very specific type of food - flowers from the plant known as pollen trumpet, a long-lived decorative plant that was created to be in symbiosis with the butterfly. If they can't find pollen trumpets nearby, they will resort to eating farm crops nearby.

A disgusting genetically modified hyena with reptilian characteristics. They prefer to feed on already dead animals, although if no corpses are present they will resort to hunting prey or consuming butchered meat.\n\n.Erins will receive a considerable health boost if consuming fresh corpses that they didn't have to kill, making them both great at corpse disposal and as front line attackers if they are properly fed. Furthermore, they have the ability to regurgitate stomach acids as a dangerous ranged attack.

A genetically modified experiment originally designed for synthread-web production that backfired horribly. The feralisk is a dangerous predator that can quickly overrun environments if not stopped.\n\nFeralisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs stun anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

A genetically modified experiment originally designed for synthread-web production that backfired horribly. The feralisk is a dangerous predator that can quickly overrun environments if not stopped.

Feralisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs stun anything they touch, allowing them to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

This feralisk is larger than usual, and is carrying a clutch of eggs on its back. This sounds like a recipe for disaster if not dealt with quickly.

A predatory creature that feed on burning flesh and vegetation. Fire wasps are not dangerous for humans, though they may prey on pets. The danger comes from their eggs, whether fertilized or not - they constantly produce an intense heat that can cause fires in the vicinity.

An example of human genetic engineering gone wrong. The objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a strange side effect - when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.\n\nRapid successive fission events are harmful to the creature. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

An example of human genetic engineering gone wrong. The objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a strange side effect - when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are harmful to the creature. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

This is a second generation fission mouse, indicating the fission process has happened once recently, making it weaker.

An example of human genetic engineering gone wrong. The objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is a sterile creature with neither attribute, but a strange side effect - when the animal dies, three duplicates are created, sharing all memories of its parent.

Rapid successive fission events are harmful to the creature. If less than a few years pass between events, the mouse eventually perishes, unable to sustain its life cycle.

This is a third generation fission mouse, indicating the fission process has happened twice recently, making it weaker. A third fission event will kill the creature for good.

A failed genetic creation that will erupt in a flaming conflagration when it dies, leaving a fire-resistant egg behind. This egg will soon hatch into a new specimen. Sometimes two eggs will be produced, this being the only viable way of reproduction the species has.

A large flightless bird adapted to living in very cold terrains. Dense plumage covers its body, keeping it warm and protected from intense winds. Unlike their more common meadow ave relatives, frost aves are slightly larger and are ovoviviparous, which let their eggs develop embryos while still inside the mother's body. The eggs remain inside her until they are ready to hatch.\n\nFrost aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

A large arthropod that is a distant relative of the smaller frostmite, sharing many similarities in its body plan, though none of their carrion eating habits. It is a creature adapted to extreme low temperatures, feeding on half inorganic vegetation present in propane lakes. Its low metabolism makes it a very efficient creature, which allows it to survive in such environments.\n\nIt is generally peaceful, and produces a blueish liquid that can be used as a milk substitute, so they are considered a nice farm animal for cold climates.

Perhaps a distant offshoot or an evolutionary relative of the nightling, the frostling is a predator adapted to extremely low temperatures. They are nocturnal animals that prey on creatures inhabiting frozen wastelands.

A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the frost lynx shares its genetic template with the genix, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.\n\nThe frost lynx was modified with hydrofluorocarbon-laced hemoglobin in its blood, allowing it to survive in extremely low temperatures, with a core body heat that would normally kill most creatures. As such, it is capable of using its low body heat to cause frostbite wounds in its victims, quickly incapacitating them. It can produce a ranged spit projectile containing particles of its blood, which can explode on impact and cover an area in frozen crystals.
A large parasite usually found in cold places. They sweep the cold barren lands in search of corpses buried in the snow, eating the preserved flesh and leaving a ravaged skeleton in its place.

A bloated, shambling corpse animated by a genetically modified strain of caterpillar fungus that was used as a biological weapon. Fungal husks serve as ambulatory delivery systems for the fungus, attempting to reach and maul any living animals nearby to spread the fungal infection.\n\nThe infection is virulent, able to kill a human in a few hours. However, it is easy to treat, and it will be kept contained and disappear as long as it is treated fast and effectively. The fungus has mutated from its original weaponized effects, and the infected won't transform into another fungal husk.

A massive, powerful, and deeply intelligent creature that can somehow ascertain when they are close to death. They'll instinctively direct themselves to an arid shrubland known as the gallatross graveyard, and die there alone, far from their group. A gallatross might expend as long as two decades roaming around a graveyard.

A massive, powerful, and deeply intelligent creature that can somehow ascertain when they are close to death. They'll instinctively direct themselves to an arid shrubland known as the gallatross graveyard, and die there alone, far from their group. A gallatross might expend as long as two decades roaming around a graveyard.\n\nThis gallatross knows it's nearing death and is preparing to die alone.

A genetically altered hybrid of a lynx and a snow leopard, the genix shares its genetic template with the frost lynx, both having diverged due to environmental pressure after their creation.\n\nThe genix is usually found on milder climates, as it has a complex biological refrigeration system that allows it to decrease ambient temperature wherever it goes. If domesticated, this strange ability can be used to refrigerate an enclosed space. The genix can explode if it receives too much damage, making it a fragile creature.

A large flightless bird that was genetically modified to produce both edible eggs and a valuable silk-like textile. A versatile farm animal, perfectly domesticated and shows very little aggression.\n\nIt is not uncommon to see flocks of giant crowned silkies grazing in pastures all along the rim. They are not usually found in the wild, and when they are, there is often a tale of violence behind them roaming around unprotected.

An ideal pack beast that have pneumatized bones, meaning they have hollow spaces within them. These light and sturdy bones let them carry more weight than their body mass would usually allow.\n\nThe gigantelope has a variable carrying capacity, set by their genome at birth, and colonies have been breeding gigantelopes for decades to try amd achieve the perfect specimen.

An armored worm known for its unquenchable appetite. Once a great devourer arrives, it will proceed to gorge itself on small prey and total ecosystem collapse is almost a certainty. They won't attack large creatures, including humans, unless provoked.\n\nThey are not very resilient and are easily dispatched. However, they have slow regenerative capabilities.

An amorphous, ambulatory mass of gelatinous fluid. Although they look like individuals, in reality they are part of a greater gelatinous superorganism, with only one objective - grow and expand.\n\nThey have an ability to reproduce constantly, requiring very little sustenance, and quickly filling all available ecological niches. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A genetically modified variant of wild sheep that produces a thick grey wool that acts as a great insulator. Grey-coated mouflons were created with a specialized organ capable of amplifying human brainwaves, acting as a biological psychic harmonizer.\n\nIf the mouflon is happy, it will provide a mood bonus to nearby human beings. Inversely, if the mouflon is suffering, it will psychically harm everyone around it.

A hybridization of a bear and mole, groundrunners originally came from mineral-planets. They are used as walking heavy tools by the locals when they hit parts that plasteel can’t break, and for hauling large boulders that their owners can’t lift. Due to their domesticated origins, they are surprisingly docile and easy to tame. Their incredible strength and sharp claws allows them to break hard materials with ease.\n\nIf trained properly, groundrunners will help colonists mine rocks and minerals. Despite that, they can be quite lazy and get distracted easily.

A genetically modified strain of the leopard slug intended as a fast corpse disposal aid. The helixien constantly secretes a foul-smelling, corrosive gas that produces an uncomfortable, itchy sensation in living beings. This gas is mostly harmless, unless it comes into contact with decaying organic matter. The gas greatly accelerates corpse rotting, liberating a black putrid liquid known as corpse bile. The helixien happily feeds on this liquid sludge, although it can also feed on other organic matter if needed.\n\nThe sight of a helixien is quite revolting and watching one wallowing in a pile of human corpses is a deeply traumatizing experience.

A small, floating gelatinous creature propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter. These squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized. As a floating creature, aerofleets ignore terrain movement costs.

Aerofleets slowly produce a thick, gelatinous substance known as blue gel. This syrupy residue can be collected and refined into an energy-dense compound. The compound can be used to build powerful batteries and generators with the appropriate research.

This aerofleet seems to have been affected by prolonged exposure to the gases emanating from an ocular forest. Red pustules and blisters are appearing in its exterior membrane and its hydrogen seems to be in the process of being turned into an acidic gas.

A giant beetle genetically engineered by a mining company a long time ago. It's a peaceful farm animal that occasionally sheds metallic husks that can be used as steel, thus negating the need for heavy machinery in mining operations. As a downside, the beetle consumes a huge amount of wood from live trees.\n\nThe mining company responsible for the ironhusk beetles didn't account for this and several planets are now a barren ecological disaster.

A mutant variation of the feralisk that has adapted to living in deep, dark jungles. Some even say that the junglelisk is the progenitor of all the variants of lisks. They reproduce at a very fast rate and female junglelisks can store the genetic material to lay eggs long after they've been fertilized.\n\nJunglelisks attack by throwing huge webs at their prey. These webs stun and cover anything they touch in acid, allowing the junglelisk to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

A very large animal native to tropical regions. Named lockjaws both for their incredibly strong bite force and for the disease they transmit, which afflicts its victims with a moderate facial paralysis that makes eating extremely uncomfortable.\n\nDespite having a guillotine for a mouth, the lockjaw does not seem to be an overly aggressive creature. It prefers to prey on local wildlife rather than humans.
A locust swarm. If left unchecked, they will devour all the grass in the area.

A small insectoid genetically modified to produce small batches of luciferium extract every few days. Even though they are useful as a source of the dangerous drug, the internal processes generating the luciferium make luciferbugs prone to violent detonation if damaged.\n\nIf they detonate, it releases all the luciferium accumulating on their abdomens, subjecting any nearby creatures to dangerous exposure levels of luciferium.

An extremely large, genetically-engineered worm. Despite its incredibly intimidating size and arsenal, these huge creatures are designed to be peaceful. It was once part of the worker caste of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. It carried and moved things that its little cousins cannot.\n\nWhile generally peaceful, if provoked, it becomes a terrifying force that can rival those of mechanoid centipedes. Originally, the mammoth worm was specifically bred to destroy mechanoid structures, and as such it can be extremely effective against buildings. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.

A mobile plant that was created as an attempt to weaponize venus flytraps by implanting concentrated formic acid spit launchers on its jaws. This strong acid is sometimes powerful enough to corrode the plasteel on mechanoid carapaces.

Usually a miserable, weak creature that oozes pus and struggles to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a genetic horror manages to survive, and even thrive. Perhaps it was released into the wild, where it managed to stabilize and grow. Or it subdued and devoured its creators. In any case, it has now turned into a pulsating, fleshy behemoth with a ravenous appetite.\n\nMature genetic horrors swallow their prey whole, storing up to 5 creatures in its huge stomach for later consumption. Prey can survive for up to one day, but they'll later be consumed and expelled as skeletonized remains.

A large flightless bird with colorful feathers that are mostly found in the plains eating fruits and berries. Because of their wildly colorful plumage, meadow aves naturally attract the eyes and hands of those who wander by. Many forget that underneath the majestic feathery coat is a wild animal with a razor sharp beak and claws to match.\n\nMeadow aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

A large genetically engineered pill bug. These creatures once served as the frontline skirmishers of a genetically modified insectoid hive made as a weapon against mechanoid invasions. Their job consisted of reducing lone mechanoid infantry to shreds. Even centipedes were no match against the swarm of spikes.\n\nNowadays, they can be found roaming in packs much smaller than their former numbers and with killer instincts that yearn to be reawakened once more. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.

A repulsive creature genetically modified to fill a very specific niche - eating metals. The tentacles in its mouth secrete an organic substance that is capable of rusting and dissolving most common metals, turning them into small flakes that serve as sustenance. They prefer small chunks of metal, since they can be more easily digested, but they will resort to digging into rocks in search of new metal if there is none available. Presumably, they were created to get rid of scrap metal, but they are mostly found in the wild now.

A ravenous, animalistic being created by genetically modifying humans so intensely, they are no longer human. Mimes are psionically gifted parasites, using their mental powers to disguise themselves as normal humans. They infiltrate human communities and live among its members for weeks, months, or even years.\n\nTheir voracious appetites cause them to constantly consume the easily available food provided by a stable colony. They will only resort to directly attacking their hosts when the food runs out.

A distant relative of the nightling. They are not as fierce as the nightling nor are they proficient hunters, often scavenging in packs for scraps left behind by predators. Their most distinctive features are the elongated structures on their snouts, which produce specific vibrational sequences that allow for discrete communication between pack members. Their physical weakness is compensated for with above average intellect, allowing them to outsmart many types of animals.\n\nA murkling can spread the bubonic plague upon biting living creatures. The delicate tendrils on their snouts can dissolve nearby corpses and turn them into semi-liquid carrion that they can consume.

A variant of the overgrown colossus native to mycotic jungles. They are reptilian in nature, with cold blood and a slow metabolism. They have six legs, two intertwined spines, and six eyes.

It has a symbiotic relationship with fungi, with several mutant agarilux mushrooms growing on its back. These fungi trap insects and seem to provide sustenance in a symbiotic relationship with the colossus.

This colossus reproduces by sporulation, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

When tamed, the mycoid colossus can be periodically trimmed to obtain raw agarilux mushrooms.

A cactus genetically modified to be given sentience. It was given a mobile body, an infantile intelligence, and toxic barbs. Needleposts can derive nutrition from very small amounts of rotting vegetables but they need a huge amount of sunlight over anything else. Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse is usually fatal to them.

Needlerolls are needleposts that have evolved to grow in extremely arid and dry environments. Needlerolls need almost no sustenance, absorbing all the energy they need from sunlight and minute amounts of water that they extract from morning dew. They need a huge amount of sunlight. Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse could be fatal to them.

A hardy pack beast used for transporting loads or doing other heavy work. Nightmules originated from a mysterious rimworld orbiting a very faint star, so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. They were domesticated by an elusive race called the forsaken hundreds of years ago and can be found roaming around other planets.\n\nNightmules are stronger than muffalos, though they produce a very low amount of milk and no wool. Their back is crowned by dangerous quills, though they lack the capacity to throw them as defensive weapons.

A large flightless bird that is as black as the night. Night aves originated from a mysterious rimworld orbiting a very faint star, so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight and are purely nocturnal animals.\n\nNight aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

A sleek predatory beast with rows of quills on its back. The nightling is a purely nocturnal hunter and will prey on much larger animals than itself. Apart from its strong jaws, nightlings can throw the quills on their backs to overpower their prey.

A stubborn herbivore that shares much of its genome with the predatory nightling. The nightram originated from a mysterious rimworld orbiting a very faint star, so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. They were domesticated by an elusive race called the forsaken hundreds of years ago.\n\nWhen found on other worlds, the nightram are exclusively nocturnal, instinctively avoiding natural sunlight. Nightrams are peaceful unless disturbed or threatened.

An animal that seems to have some biological similarities with aerofleet, being filled with a buoyant gas, but its effects on terrestrial ecosystems are unusual. The creature releases clouds of reddish gas that is harmless to animals. However, when flora is exposed to it, it mutates and turns into strange specimens that share 98% of its genome with the jelly. This flora is almost inedible and its relationship with the ocular jelly remains as of yet unexplained. As a floating creature, ocular jellies ignore terrain movement costs. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.
A mutated nightling created by infusing the animal with strange energies from an extra-dimensional corruption. Sturdier and more docile than normal nightlings.

The overgrown colossus is a gargantuan beast that arose naturally in some remote swamp-filled planet. They are reptilian in nature, with cold blood and a slow metabolism. They have six legs, two intertwined spines, and six eyes.

It has a symbiotic relationship with vegetation, with several small trees growing on its back. These trees photosynthesize and help provide nutrients for the overgrown colossus.

When tamed, the overgrown colossus can be periodically trimmed to obtain wood.

Pebblemits are bouldermits that have evolved in narrow, labyrinthine caves, where massive size is more a hindrance than an advantage. Instead of huge boulders, pebblemits use much smaller rocks as protection, slowly dragging them along the ground. Small blocks of stone periodically get loose from those rocks.

A genetically reconstructed dromaeosaurid commissioned by bored glitterworld elites as a symbol of status and wealth. These beasts are made to compete in judged events where the owners win titles depending on how well their animals conform to their breeds standards.\n\nWhen set loose, the raptors are usually short-lived since they depend on their human owners for survival. Their violent instincts having been bred out of them long ago. However, they are excellent companions and quite pretty.

A genetically modified feline with avian characteristics, the phoenix owlcat was created as a durable alternative to fragile baseline cats. A loyal companion that isn't as easily hunted by hostile predators. The ancient folklore of cats having nine lives was used as a pattern to create the phoenix owlcat. A swarm of powerful mechanites in its bloodstream is capable of saving it from up to 9 lethal wounds before being lost to decoherence.

A mutant snail that has an armored shell made of iron sulphide and specialized organs that generate an electric discharge similar to those found in electric eels. This discharge is very low voltage, not powerful enough to damage most creatures. However, the plasmorph uses it as a spark to ignite its own flammable spit and lob it at its prey.\n\nSuch a strange mechanism is surely not natural, but what its intended purpose was is a mystery lost to the ages.

A peaceful herbivore bred to thrive in high radiation environments. Its digestive tract is composed of six bionic stomachs reinforced with a lead-lined biolattice designed to extract residual radioactive material from grass cells. This radioactive material is deposited in crystal-like formations that pierce the hard skin of the creature. These crystals can be harvested periodically and refined into uranium in a standard chemfuel refinery.\n\nThe technology behind creating such carefully engineered creatures is completely out of reach in most societies, so a radyak is a valued acquisition.

A large genetically modified creature that is known to make homes in tropical regions and are very territorial.

Bullets struggle to pierce its thick armor and its sharp claws can slice limbs clean off.

Raptor shrimps have impressive regenerative capabilities and shouldn't be considered dead until they unmistakably are.

A large genetically-engineered insectoid that is a part of the black hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The ravager was conceived as a space-bound bioweapon. Drop pods would be filled with ravagers and launched towards mechanoid ships. The insectoids would rip through the ship's plating and destroy any mechanoid inside. Ravagers proved to be too unreliable and the geneline was scrapped.\n\nSeveral ravagers can be seen in derelict spaceships, stations, and asteroids, as well as aimlessly roaming the countryside. They are mostly adapted to their solitary life in space. These insects can cause additional damage to mechanoids.

A genetically engineered species based on the black and white tegu, with several traits from the electric eel. The pair of fleshy tentacles extending from a ray-hound's skull are electrogenic and are used as a defense mechanism against predators. An electrical discharge from a ray-hound's tentacles can easily disable electronic circuits.\n\nRay-hounds make amenable pets, as they tend to become acclimated to their owners and are generally quite docile as adults.

An aggressive and adaptable creature with a dual-jawed mouth that leads to two separate but intertwined digestive systems, each of them adapted to consume different types of food. This arrangement makes them extremely energy-efficient. Razorjacks can live in the most desolate conditions since their need for nutrients is very low.\n\nAlthough it might seem canine at first, its genome has more in common with rodents, with some unusual genetic splicing thrown into the mix. Wounds caused by Razorjacks tend to get infected very easily.

A blob of bubbling organic matter that seems to be an extension of the terrain itself, a disfigured excrescence given a semblance of life.\n\nThe red goo seem to thrive in the bizarre environment of the ocular forest, nibbling on the aberrant vegetation and periodically cloning itself. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A strange creature of unknown origin. It isn't carbon based, instead using gallium as the basis of its structure and life functions. This is considered physically impossible under normal circumstances, so the red spore may come from a place where the rules are wildly different from this universe.\n\nThe red spore is inherently unstable, with a low lifespan, prone to violent explosions, and unable to reproduce normally. As a floating creature, red spores ignore terrain movement costs.

A purely biological defense weapon created to fight against insectoids. They sport two viciously sharp claws specially designed to attach to chitinous plates and rip them apart.\n\nDespite their fearsome appearance, ripper hounds can be extremely affectionate and loyal. They love to be pet by those they trust.

A large monitor lizard adapted to life in extreme conditions. Their whole body and metabolism are adapted to environments of higher than normal acidity, thriving around acidic volcanic lakes with a water pH of 2 to 3. This immunity to acid allows them to prey on other creatures that use acid to deter predators.\n\nThe rough-plated monitor lays highly acidic eggs that, when hatching, can suddenly explode.

A large flightless bird with colorful feathers. Royal aves are meadow aves that underwent selective crossbreeding to reduce their stubbornness and increase their fluffiness. Some of these prized pets get freed into the wild, a life that they are poorly adapted for. Plumage on royal aves are more flamboyant than a regular meadow ave and can rarely showcase an entire rainbow of color on their feathers.\n\nRoyal aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses. If properly trained, they can be ridden into battle at incredible speeds.

A variant of the genetically modified arctic lion, specifically engineered as ambush units in extreme high temperature environments. The sand lion has the ability to constantly digging into sand, producing dense clouds of particulate matter that obscures line of sight of its prey, making it easier for the lion to attack them.

A genetic amalgamation possessing features of a lion, a shark and a sand skink. It was originally created as a ferocious hunting animal for desert planets. The sand prowler can burrow into and swim through loose sand, hiding the bulk of its body and allowing it to strike its prey from relative safety.

A genetically modified creature that incorporates features from both cephalopods and cone snails. Sand squids were cattle created to adapt to extremely water deprived environments, such as very dry deserts.\n\nThe sand squid constantly produces a sticky secretion that acts as a powerful fertilizer when mixed with common sand, allowing the growth of crops in the middle of the desert. It can be trained to properly distribute its slime around fields to increase terrain fertility even more.

A creature known for its mighty elongated horns. It is passive and their horns will only be used upon provocation or during mating. Their name is derived from their aggression against potential rivals during mating season, where the females are seen charging and locking horns with each other to secure a mate.\n\nWhile they were once used as battle mounts due to their speed and ability to ram, nowadays they are mostly reared for their creamy milk and abundant meat.

Shock goats are domesticated cattle known for their capacity to store static electricity on their bony structures and can release it as a defensive measure. They are commonly seen in farming communities because they produce decent amounts of milk and can defend themselves well.

An animal created using the DNA from an animus vox spliced into the genome of a companion dog to create a creature that is capable of psionically detecting the wishes of its master. This was only partially realized and skiphounds will uncontrollably use their latent psionic powers to blink in and out of existence, making them extremely unpredictable.\n\nSkiphounds will always use their psionic power unless eating or sleeping. An attacking skiphound will rapidly teleport close to its prey, rendering defenses such as barricades and walls completely useless.

A space-borne creature that inhabits the asteroids of a system's asteroid belt. They are usually not found on a planet's surface unless they are somehow brought to it. Their bodies are light and they have no problems flying through a terrestrial atmosphere. They also have electricity based defense mechanisms and a faint regenerative ability.\n\nArcturan sky eels require very little sustenance and can be trained as simple pets.

A modified bio-mechanoid capable of devouring almost anything and processing it into a homogeneous organic slurry. This slurry is barely edible for carnivorous and omnivorous animals and completely indigestible for herbivores. Slurrypedes are docile, almost never hostile, and if a mechanoid base is destroyed and one of them manages to survive, they tend to roam the wilderness, consuming any organic material in their path and turning it into nutrient paste.
A farm animal with cow and goat characteristics, bred to survive in extreme environments. Spined gows are herbivorous, happy to graze in any grassy meadow. Spìned gows provide a very nutritious milk.

Swarmlings were one of humanity's first successful genetic engineering creations, bred to enrich the biosphere of Mars, until they hitched a ride aboard an interstellar-bound colony ship. Swarmlings are never found alone. They are an asexual species that reproduce by attacking another creature, implanting larvae in it. The larvae hatch once the creature has died.

A menacing-looking beast that might seem to be a truly alien creature. In reality, it was artificially created as living waste disposal. The tar guzzler creeps along parched mud with six strong tentacles, avidly searching for its favourite food - puddles of viscous tar.\n\nTar guzzlers have a very limited intelligence and they don't have any natural predators, so they are usually just left alone.

An amorphous, flesh coloured, translucent creature that lacks everything but the most basic instincts. It moves around slowly and sometimes devours plants it comes in contact with, incorporating it into its cytoplasm. There are some chunks of seemingly normal flesh floating inside it.\n\nTeratogenic originators are an enormous clonal colony of pluripotent stem cells, capable of differentiating into different tissues. They were engineered by a group of unethical scientists as a cheap way to create lab-grown limbs suitable for transplants but the end results is less than ideal. These strange mutant limbs can be periodically excised from the creature and used at will. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.

A strange looking crustacean that was created with the intention to process minerals. They can feed on steel compounds and process them chemically to slowly turn them into sky steel, a type of material that is normally only found in asteroids.\n\nThe transmutation process is very slow, so it needs to spend a lot of time surrounded by steel. It can also slowly consume, but not convert, steel slag chunks.

A common sight among glitterworld territories, where they lumber about as glorified power plants. Outside of those terrories, they are deployed as a mobile power source for glitterworld research expeditions. Their bodily chemical composition is capable of outputting power that far surpasses any known natural sources. Thus, they are widely valued by every technologically developing civilization throughout the galaxy.\n\nWhile they would prefer to run away instead of fight, modified slugs are armored with plasteel shells, quad cores that can act as tesla cannons, and a tactical AI inserted within the brain that takes over and makes no hesitation to use all of its armament to obliterate any perceived threat nearby. Properly outfitted tetra slugs will slowly recharge batteries in their vicinity.

A large blackspider that has been biologically augmented with volatile chemical glands. Originally, it was bred by the creators of the black hive as a fearsome fire-breathing shock trooper, using thermal grenades capable of affecting mechanoids. They managed to quickly adapt to these biological grenades. The thermadon project was abandoned and they were released into the wild.

A swine-like mammal capable of generating large electric currents. It has a specialized nervous system that can synchronize the activity of disc-shaped, electricity-producing cells inside a specialized organ.\n\nThough they were initially created to serve as a way to generate bio-electricity, thunderbeasts have naturally evolved over the centuries making them extremely unstable. They can release jolts of electricity at great distances and will negatively affect weather if they are slaughtered. Predators usually give them a wide berth.

A creature often seen in colder environments, it is recognized by its shaggy thick fur and stumpy but effective horn. They get their name from their tendency to bray out during the dawn of thunderstorms, which is used as a signal by farmers and drifters alike to seek refuge. They are reared in cold wastelands for their thick milk, comfortable fur, and tough but satiating meat.\n\nThunderox are resilient beasts and can slowly regenerate their health.

A variant of wildpods that have adapted to life outside of swamps and rainforests. Since they have less access to water and rotting vegetation, they grow much less, and are much less dangerous. Wildpawns are less resistant to gunfire than wildpods but still retain the weakness to fire. Wildpawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.\n\nWildpawns can be hunted or farmed for small amounts of edible raw fungus.

A lumbering, sentient mycoid creature. The wildpod is almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass. In contrast, they are very weak to fire. Wildpods reproduces asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are completely wild and independent of it, with no concept of parenthood. Asexual creatures like this one can't be sterilized.\n\nAlthough risky, wildpods can be hunted or farmed for decent amounts of edible raw fungus.

A rare mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with fleshy tentacles housing a distributed net of weather-affecting mechanites.\n\nThese deployable mechanite swarms have the ability to affect the weather in a localized manner, creating pressure gradients that may evolve into full-blown hurricane winds. This effect is used offensively by the creature and is especially dangerous if it is killed, as the large sudden release of all mechanites can cause a tornado. Predators usually give them a wide berth.
A grey-coated mouflon nearby is angry or hurt, creating psychic waves of agony that are extremely distracting...
